findings.title: `.json` task files are parsed with the YAML loader, so valid JSON is silently altered or refused
findings.claim: A `tasks: file.json` task file is not read as JSON. JSON numbers with an exponent but no '.' or no exponent sign are silently sealed as strings, a raw U+0085 inside a JSON string is silently folded to a space, and two kinds of valid JSON are refused outright (tab indentation; surrogate-pair escapes, which Python's default `json.dump` emits for any emoji or other non-BMP character). The same content in a `.jsonl` file is read correctly, so the same task set compiles to different task content and a different experiment_id depending only on the file extension. The agent then receives `"1e-05"` where the author wrote `1e-05`.

findings.title: Any unreadable or invalid neighbouring `*/manifest.json` aborts a suite run with an error that names `prior_runs` and not the offending file
findings.claim: Prior-run discovery reads every `<out>/*/manifest.json`. A neighbour that is not valid JSON, is not UTF-8, is a suite manifest with a broken seal, or is an incomplete suite manifest stops `arci run` (exit 3) even when it belongs to an unrelated suite or is an arbitrary directory. The message points at the descriptor key `prior_runs`, which the user did not write, and for every non-OSError case does not say which directory is bad, so with several run directories in the shared default `runs/` there is nothing to act on. One case prints a multi-kilobyte raw pydantic dump with documentation URLs. Refusing is a defensible choice; the unusable message is the defect (brief: every error names the key and the fix).

findings.title: prior_runs discovery under-reports earlier runs in four reproducible cases
findings.claim: (1) A neighbour's own `prior_runs` are not carried forward, so once an earlier run directory is pruned (for example a CI cache that keeps only the latest run) that run disappears from the new manifest. (2) A suite run whose manifest has its `schema_version` value altered is silently skipped, and (3) so is a run directory whose `manifest.json` is gone while its trials remain, although plan-notes/AGENT_SEMANTICS_suite_section.md states 'Malformed prior manifests are refused rather than silently omitted' and a broken seal in the same file is refused. (4) With an empty candidate_id the match is whole-ArmSpec equality, so changing only the candidate's `label` drops all earlier runs of the same agent. Discovery itself keys on validated file content, not directory names (a copy under another directory name is still found once), which is right; it does not require the directory name to equal the id or any trials to exist, so a sealed manifest alone counts as a prior run, which errs on the side of disclosure.
